section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section contains the header and date of the maamar.
section.t: With the help of Heaven*.
15 Tammuz,

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that while even one person studying Torah draws down Divinity, the drawing down through Torah study of many is a loftier revelation, analogous to the superiority of communal prayer which draws down the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy beyond the chain of descent, and even beyond proportion to the arousal from below.
section.t: "Ten who sit and engage in Torah, the Shechinah dwells among them"1,
and it is explained by the Rebbe, my father-in-law, the Rebbe of the Geulah, in his maamar beginning with the words "Zeh" that was given on the occasion of the first Yud-Beis Tammuz celebration
(the year 5688),
that even one who sits and engages in Torah draws down a revelation of G-dliness,
as per the continuation of the Mishnah: "And from where [do we learn] even five... even three... even two... even one...",
nevertheless,
the drawing down through the Torah of many is a more elevated drawing down.
For just as regarding prayer our Sages, of blessed memory, said2
"The prayer of the many is not rejected,"
because through the prayer of the many, the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy that are above the chain of descent are drawn down,
and moreover3
the drawing down from above through the prayer of the many is not commensurate with their arousal from below
(even not commensurate with the arousal from below of the many),
so too is it regarding Torah,
that through the Torah study of many, there is a drawing down of the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy that are above the chain of descent
[For although the drawing down of the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy through engaging in Torah is due to the virtue of Torah,
that the Thirteen Attributes by which the Torah is expounded correspond to the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy.
From this it is understood,
that the drawing down of the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy also occurs when one sits and engages in Torah,
nevertheless, the drawing down of the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy through engaging in Torah is primarily specifically through Torah study in public,
meaning that the level of the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy that is drawn down through engaging in Torah in public is a more elevated level],
and moreover,
the drawing down through the Torah study of many is not commensurate with the study of the many.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the parallel between Torah and prayer is hinted at in the Mishnah's verse about the Temple, connecting the place of the Shechinah, the mention of the explicit Name, and the service of offerings and prayer, showing Torah and prayer are interrelated in this specific matter.
section.t: And it can be said,
that the analogy of Torah to prayer,
is also hinted at in the aforementioned Mishnah: "And from where [do we learn] even one? As it is said4
'In every place where I cause My name to be mentioned, I will come to you and bless you,'"
"In every place etc." refers to the Holy Temple
[a place where the Shechinah comes,
"I will come to you"],
where permission was given to mention the explicit Name
["I cause My name to be mentioned"]5,
and the Holy Temple is related to the pillar of service,
offerings6
and prayer7
[And to add,
that even the Priestly Blessing, in which they would mention the Name as it is written in the Holy Temple5,
was after the offering of the daily morning sacrifice8
(the beginning of all the offerings),
and also now the Sages instituted the Priestly Blessing in prayer9,
and within the prayer itself – in the blessing of the service10].
And in the Mishnah, this verse is brought
("In every place where I cause My name to be mentioned, I will come to you and bless you")
regarding the dwelling of the Shechinah through Torah study,
and from this it is implied that Torah and prayer are related to each other, and specifically in this matter.
